cite: Harris (1913), Factory 10(2), read in the 1990 reprint p. 948
quote: the value for X that will give the minimum value to Y, reduces to the square root of (240MS divided by C).
paraphrase: Harris writes the lot size that keeps the combined set-up and carrying cost lowest as a square root, with M the monthly movement, S the set-up cost and C the unit cost; the 240 folds together the twelve months of a year and his ten per cent a year for interest and depreciation.

cite: Harris (1913), Factory 10(2), read in the 1990 reprint p. 948
quote: Applying the formula, it is found that the theoretical economical size of lot is 2,190 units.
paraphrase: His first worked example, a movement of 1,000 units a month, a set-up cost of two dollars and a unit cost of ten cents, gives a lot he prints as 2,190.

cite: Harris (1913), Factory 10(2), read in the 1990 reprint p. 949
quote: The correct quantity is 48.5 or, say, 49.
paraphrase: For the stud of his Figure III he prints the lot and then rounds it to a whole number, a rounding rule stated in words.

cite: Harris (1913), Factory 10(2), read in the 1990 reprint p. 950
quote: it is of value to know that this consumption must increase four fold to warrant doubling the manufacturing quantities.
paraphrase: Because the lot grows with the square root of demand, the demand must rise four times over before the lot doubles.

quote: In the case of redundant equipments, the R(t) might be desired in terms of the probability of r or fewer failures in time t.
paraphrase: The handbook states the chance that no more than a stated number of failures happen in a stated time, which is the Poisson cumulative probability.

quote: A slide projector is needed for 500 hours of operation. Replacement of failed lamps is permitted, but there are only two spare bulbs on hand.
paraphrase: The handbook example holds two spares for a mission of a stated length.

quote: If the lamp failure rate is 0.001 failures per hour, what is the reliability for the mission (i.e., the probability that no more than two lamp failures will occur)?
paraphrase: With a stated failure rate, the question is the chance that the two spares are enough for the whole mission.
